Day trips

Marseille

The Phocaean city, the oldest in France, offers a captivating blend of culture, history and the Mediterranean — just 30 minutes from Cassis.

30 min by car from Cassis

Marseille is a city to be experienced. From the Vieux-Port to the Panier quarter, from outstanding museums to wild calanques, every street corner tells 2 600 years of history. Make the most of your stay in Cassis to spend a day discovering this Mediterranean metropolis.

Things to see

The must-sees

Heritage, museums, nature and food — Marseille has it all.

The Panier quarter

The oldest quarter of Marseille — and of France. Narrow lanes, street art, artists' studios, independent shops and the majestic Vieille Charité. A village within the city.

Allow 2 to 3 hours to explore on foot

The Mucem

The Museum of European and Mediterranean Civilisations — spectacular architecture by Rudy Ricciotti. Permanent collections and temporary exhibitions in an iconic waterfront building.

Mucem official website

Fort Saint-Jean

A 17th-century fortress commissioned by Louis XIV, guarding the entrance to the Vieux-Port. Linked to the Mucem by a spectacular footbridge. The Jardin des Migrations, stunning viewpoints over the city and the sea — and entry is free.

Free entry — Footbridge to the Mucem
Our favourite

Cosquer Méditerranée

An immersive replica of the Cosquer cave, discovered beneath the sea in the calanques. 33 000-year-old cave art, explored aboard self-driving pods. A unique, spectacular experience for the whole family.

18 € adults · 11 € (ages 10-17) · 6 € (ages 6-9)
Book online

The calanques of Marseille

Sormiou and Morgiou, the big sisters of the Cassis calanques. Car access is restricted in season, so it's best to walk in. Breathtaking scenery and swimming in wild coves.

Limited car access in summer — MesCalanques app recommended

Notre-Dame de la Garde

The ‘Bonne Mère’ (Good Mother), Marseille's guardian, towers over the city at 154 metres above sea level. 360° panorama over the city, the port, the Frioul islands and the calanques. Free entry.

By car, bus or on foot — Free entry
